subject.title: Bug: Gateway falsely marks healthy local vLLM endpoints as timed out/overloaded, causing 1–23 min fallback cascades

question: Should this stay as the broad live-repro tracker for local-vLLM gateway timeout cascades, or should maintainers split the remaining work into narrower timeout, stall-detection, fallback, and RPC-latency issues after a current-main trace?
rationale: The source and related PRs prove several partial repairs, but the remaining behavior crosses provider routing, local model timeout policy, cron/live-session state, auth prewarm, gateway RPC responsiveness, and session recovery; choosing the next owner boundary is maintainer intent, not a safe deterministic cleanup decision.

options.title: Capture current-main trace first
options.body: Keep this issue open and require a live local-vLLM trace before choosing a code fix or closing any part of the cluster.

options.title: Split after trace
options.body: Use this issue to collect proof, then move confirmed remaining defects to narrower canonical issues such as local silent-model stall policy or fallback-chain timeout exhaustion.

options.title: Close only after proof
options.body: Close this issue only if a current-main live run shows the original false-timeout and `sessions_spawn` latency cascade no longer occurs.

recommendation.title: Capture current-main trace first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require a live local-vLLM trace before choosing a code fix or closing any part of the cluster.

likelyOwner.reason: osolmaz is assigned to the issue and has already made the maintainer decision for the adjacent cron fallback semantics, making them the best available routing owner for the next boundary choice.
